nodes.content: Design an ownership type checker for cancellable asynchronous tasks that safely transfer borrowed resources across task boundaries.
requirements: Guarantee memory safety under cancellation and task migration without whole-program analysis or runtime borrow checks.
Accept 12 safe and reject 12 unsafe programs covering nested borrows, ownership transfer, and cancellation.

nodes.content: Build a modular region-and-effect checker with region-indexed affine task handles, scoped reborrows, Send migration bounds, and cancel-and-join teardown.
What handle-region rule rejects detaching tasks with borrowed captures while permitting moved-owned captures to outlive the spawning scope?
Requiring owned Send+'static detached captures and region-bounded cancel-and-join for scoped borrows should classify all 24 BorrowTask cases.
Implement checker prototype and run BorrowTask’s 12 safe and 12 unsafe cases across nested reborrows, detach, cancellation, and migration.
BorrowTask v0.1 accepted 12/12 safe and rejected 12/12 unsafe cases across reborrows, cancellation, detachment, and migration.
Adopt the handle-region rule for scoped borrows and owned Send+'static detach captures; BorrowTask passed all 24 cases.
Prove compositional preservation and progress for the adopted handle-region rule and cancel-and-join teardown under migration; expand BorrowTask transfer regressions.
Mechanize preservation and scheduler-aware progress for handle-region cancellation and migration; add six nested-transfer cases to BorrowTask.
BorrowTask-Coq v0.2 contains modular preservation and scheduler-step progress proofs plus 30 fixtures, including six nested ownership-transfer regressions.
Extract BorrowTask-Coq v0.2 semantics and enumerate cancellation-before-join and migration schedules across 30 fixtures, checking preservation and progress.
BorrowTask-Coq accepted 15/15 safe and rejected 15/15 unsafe fixtures; 480 bounded cancellation/migration schedules showed zero invariant violations.
Using BorrowTask-Coq v0.2, type-check opaque task APIs separately and enumerate cancellation/migration schedules for captured nested borrows.
Opaque API summaries omitted child-task obligations: checker accepted an unsafe nested transfer; owner dropped before child teardown in 3/96 schedules.
Retain region-indexed handles for visible tasks, but reject opaque APIs unless summaries expose transitive child-task teardown obligations.
Use modular task-capability summaries tracking transitive borrows, Send constraints, and child cancel-and-join obligations across opaque APIs.
How can opaque task-capability summaries preserve transitive child teardown obligations without rejecting safe ownership transfers through generic wrappers?
Region-polymorphic affine child-join summaries should accept safe generic-wrapper transfers and eliminate the 3/96 owner-before-child teardown failures.
Implement region-polymorphic affine child-join summaries and rerun 96 opaque-API schedules plus BorrowTask fixtures with generic-wrapper transfers.
Region-polymorphic summaries accepted 4/4 safe wrappers, rejected the prior opaque counterexample, and preserved teardown across 96 permitted schedules.
Prove region-polymorphic summary soundness under cancellation and migration; test 12 safe and 12 unsafe cross-module programs.
Mechanize summary-substitution preservation under cancellation and migration in BorrowTask-Coq; check CrossModule-24’s 12 safe and 12 unsafe programs.
BorrowTask-Coq v0.3 contains cancellation/migration summary-substitution preservation proofs and CrossModule-24’s 12 safe and 12 unsafe cross-module programs.
Add affine resource-escrow tokens to task summaries, releasing borrowed owners only after transitive child joins under cancellation.
Can escrow tokens remain affine when cancellation races child completion across migrating workers?
Affine escrow tokens transferred at spawn and consumed after transitive joins should prevent double-release in cancellation/completion migration races.
Extend BorrowTask-Coq v0.3 with escrow transitions and enumerate cancellation/completion races across two migrating workers on CrossModule-24.
Across 768 two-worker race schedules, no escrow token double-released; CrossModule-24 accepted 12/12 safe and rejected 12/12 unsafe.
Using BorrowTask-Coq v0.3, model-check three-worker nested-child cancellation/completion races for escrow duplication and premature owner release.
Three-worker search found 2/1,536 schedules where concurrent child completion and cancellation duplicated escrow, enabling double-release before nested join.
Retain affine escrow summaries, but reject independent completion/cancellation releases; require one terminal token-consumption transition before supporting three-worker migration.
A single atomic terminal handle transition after transitive child joins should consume escrow exactly once in three-worker cancellation/completion races.
Encode terminal-transition exclusivity in BorrowTask-Coq v0.3 and rerun the 1,536 three-worker race schedules plus CrossModule-24.
With exclusive terminal transitions, 1,536 three-worker schedules showed zero duplicate releases; CrossModule-24 retained 12/12 safe acceptance and unsafe rejection.
Prove exclusive terminal-transition escrow soundness under cancellation and migration, then validate modular static checking on CrossModule-24.
Extend BorrowTask-Coq v0.3 with exclusive-terminal escrow preservation under cancellation and migration; type-check CrossModule-24 using opaque module summaries.
BorrowTask-Coq v0.4 contains exclusive-terminal escrow preservation proofs and an opaque-summary checker with CrossModule-24 regression tests.
Compile transitive escrow obligations into interface-level teardown DAGs, statically rejecting cancellation paths that drop owners before child joins.
How can finite interface teardown DAGs summarize recursive child-task creation without masking join obligations or rejecting safe programs?
SCC-folded teardown DAG templates with guarded affine child-join obligations should remain finite and classify CrossModule-24’s 24 cases.
Implement SCC-folded teardown DAG summaries in BorrowTask-Coq v0.4; measure template growth and check recursive wrappers plus CrossModule-24.
SCC-folded guarded DAGs stayed within 18 nodes across 10 recursive wrappers; CrossModule-24 accepted 12/12 safe, rejected 12/12 unsafe.
Stress BorrowTask-Coq v0.4 with mutually recursive child-spawning wrappers and cancellation-dependent guards, checking SCC template finiteness and join-order soundness.
Cancellation-dependent guards prevented SCC folding in 2/8 mutually recursive wrappers; each unfolding added a distinct affine join obligation.
Keep SCC-folded DAGs for guard-stable recursion; reject cancellation-dependent recursive wrappers unless their interfaces expose a finite join bound.
Guard-stable SCC folding plus explicit join bounds should finitely summarize bounded cancellation-dependent recursion without losing affine obligations.
Add explicit join-bound annotations to BorrowTask-Coq v0.4; recheck eight mutual-recursion wrappers and CrossModule-24 for finite DAGs.
Explicit join bounds made 8/8 mutual-recursion summaries finite, at most 24 nodes; CrossModule-24 retained 12/12 safe and unsafe classification.
Using v0.4's finite join-bound summaries, enumerate three-worker cancellation/migration schedules for eight mutual-recursion wrappers, checking affine escrow conservation.
In 2/2,048 schedules, one bounded wrapper reused a join allowance across sibling spawns, releasing escrow before both children joined.
Keep finite join-bound DAGs, but require each sibling spawn to consume a distinct affine allowance before accepting bounded recursion.
Per-spawn affine join allowances with guard-stable SCC folding should keep bounded recursive summaries finite and prevent premature escrow release.
Compare join-bound summaries against per-spawn affine allowances in BorrowTask-Coq v0.4 across eight wrappers and 2,048 race schedules.
Vector-valued join bounds, without per-spawn tokens, kept 8/8 recursive summaries finite and prevented premature release across 2,048 schedules.
Extend BorrowTask-Coq v0.4 with per-spawn allowance conservation; test dynamically spawned siblings against vector bounds under cancellation and migration.
In 3/4,096 dynamic-sibling schedules, interchangeable per-spawn allowances let one child’s join discharge another’s obligation, releasing escrow early.
Instrument BorrowTask-Coq v0.4 to trace allowance identities in dynamic-sibling races and test whether joins consume their originating child’s allowance.
Allowance traces identified cross-child consumption in all three failures; origin-matched joins eliminated premature release across 4,096 replayed schedules.
Bind each affine allowance to its spawned child’s identity; only that child’s terminal join may discharge it, preventing cross-child consumption.
Prove child-identified allowance conservation and modular teardown soundness, then rerun CrossModule-24 and 4,096 dynamic-sibling cancellation/migration schedules.
Mechanize child-identified allowance conservation and modular teardown soundness in BorrowTask-Coq v0.4; rerun CrossModule-24 and 4,096 sibling-race schedules.
BorrowTask-Coq v0.5 contains child-identified allowance conservation and modular teardown proofs, plus CrossModule-24 and 4,096-schedule sibling-race regressions.
Audit BorrowTask-Coq v0.5’s child-identity and teardown proofs; rerun CrossModule-24 and 4,096 sibling cancellation/migration schedules.
Audit found zero proof gaps; CrossModule-24 accepted 12/12 safe, rejected 12/12 unsafe, and 4,096 schedules showed zero premature releases.
Adopt child-identified join allowances over interchangeable tokens: v0.5 classified CrossModule-24 perfectly and prevented premature release across 4,096 schedules.
